periods.analysis: Fleet Electrification Pilot opened the series at 4% complete and green; there is no prior-quarter movement in this data set. Charging depot site prep is complete with dueOffsetDays -40, including conduit, concrete pads, and bollards at Public Works Yard B for chargers CHG-01 through CHG-04. The “First 6 EV pickups delivered” milestone is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35, and I am not counting those trucks until upfit, radios, and Fleet asset tags EV-PU-001 through EV-PU-006 pass acceptance. The 12-month TCO comparison report is not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, which is fine at this stage because the odometer and work-order data are not yet worth much. Green is appropriate; the pipes and the batteries both prefer boring execution.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by closing the utility energization checklist for Yard B and documenting charger commissioning readings by circuit, not by anecdote. Fleet should pre-load fuel, maintenance, and downtime baselines for the six comparable gas pickups so the TCO report has a defensible control group. Keep the pickup delivery milestone on the weekly scorecard until EV-PU-001 through EV-PU-006 have radios, decals, bed protection, and telematics accepted.

periods.analysis: Fleet Electrification Pilot moved from 4% to 7% complete, a 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. Charging depot site prep stays complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and the crews used the quarter to finish panel labeling, wheel stops, and snow-season access striping around CHG-01 through CHG-04. The “First 6 EV pickups delivered” milestone remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35 because the vehicles are still working through municipal upfit and acceptance rather than just dealer drop-off. The 12-month TCO comparison report remains not-started with dueOffsetDays 200; that is the right call until we have actual duty-cycle data from Streets, Parks, Inspections, and Utilities routes.
periods.recommendations: Maintain momentum by scheduling a joint vendor-Fleet punch walk and making any charger defects a 10-business-day correction item. Assign the first six EV pickups to fixed route cohorts so we do not compare a beach-parking truck to a valve crew truck and pretend the math is clean. Start a simple weekly exception log for charging faults, operator comments, and miles driven so the later TCO work is evidence, not folklore.

periods.analysis: The pilot advanced from 7% to 10% complete, another 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the status is still green. Site prep remains complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and Facilities verified drainage, pedestal torque, and protective clearances after the winter rain events at Yard B. The first 6 EV pickups milestone is still in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35; Fleet is holding the line on acceptance because telematics pings from EV-PU-003 and EV-PU-005 were intermittent during the first yard tests. The 12-month TCO comparison report is still not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, and I am comfortable with that because we are still building the dataset rather than decorating a report.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by requiring a signed acceptance sheet for each EV pickup that includes charger compatibility, radio operation, payload configuration, and telematics validation. Extend the pilot discipline by giving each assigned crew a one-page charging SOP and winter range note before the trucks go into daily duty. Preserve budget credibility by tagging all EV-related work orders in the Fleet system under one project code, FLEET-EV-PILOT.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 10% to 13%, a 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement, with the initiative remaining green. The depot site prep milestone remains complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and the chargers have now been folded into the Yard B preventive maintenance route with monthly visual checks and breaker temperature scans. The first 6 EV pickups delivered milestone remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35, primarily because two service bodies and one ladder rack still need final weight and clearance confirmation before I will call them city-ready. The 12-month TCO comparison report remains not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, but Fleet has enough early metering structure in place to keep the future analysis honest. This is steady work, not magic; steady work is what keeps a coastal fleet available in July.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green by completing the service-body weight checks and documenting usable payload for each of EV-PU-001 through EV-PU-006. Add charger uptime and kWh dispensed to the weekly Public Works scorecard so operations sees the equipment as assets, not furniture. Begin drafting the TCO report template now, with placeholders for depreciation, electricity, avoided fuel, maintenance labor, downtime, and residual assumptions.

periods.analysis: The pilot moved from 13% to 16% complete, a 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. Charging depot site prep is still complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and summer load checks showed no nuisance trips on CHG-01 through CHG-04 during afternoon return-to-yard charging. The first 6 EV pickups delivered milestone remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35, with the remaining work centered on final operator sign-off for Utilities, Streets, and Code Compliance assignments. The 12-month TCO comparison report remains not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, but we now have enough route discipline to know which comparisons will be fair and which will be nonsense. The program is still small, which is useful; small pilots expose bad assumptions before they become capital plans.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by running a 30-day operator acceptance window and closing comments by asset ID rather than collecting loose opinions. Extend the green result by adding a second charging-use dashboard view for peak-hour charging, after-hours charging, and failed sessions. Prepare the FY budget note now showing what evidence will be needed before Harborview buys beyond the first six pickups.

periods.analysis: Fleet Electrification Pilot advanced from 16% to 19% complete, another 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the status remains green. Depot site prep continues to be complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and the chargers made it through the first full wet-season inspection cycle without standing-water or cabinet-seal issues. The first 6 EV pickups delivered milestone is still in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35 because Fleet is resolving final acceptance details on decals, spare charging cards, and one vendor firmware update. The 12-month TCO comparison report remains not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, but fuel-card and maintenance baselines for the matched gas pickups are now clean enough to defend. That matters because Council will ask whether this is cheaper, cleaner, or just shinier; I prefer answers with units.
periods.recommendations: Keep the initiative green by closing the firmware update and confirming every assigned operator has a working charging credential before holiday staffing thins out. Extend the pilot by adding a quarterly battery-health export from the vendor portal for EV-PU-001 through EV-PU-006. Direct Finance and Fleet to agree on the TCO assumptions now, especially electricity rate, labor rate, and replacement-cycle treatment, so the report is not renegotiated after the facts arrive.

periods.analysis: Completion moved from 19% to 22%, a 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter gain, and the initiative remains green. Charging depot site prep remains complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and preventive maintenance records now tie CHG-01 through CHG-04 to the same asset-management workflow we use for pumps, signals, and generators. The first 6 EV pickups delivered milestone remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35; remaining acceptance items are administrative and configuration-related, not a sign of asset failure. The 12-month TCO comparison report is still not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, and that continues to be appropriate while the pilot accumulates a full operating year of comparable mileage, kWh, tire, brake, and downtime data. Green is earned here by restraint, not by declaring victory early.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by completing the acceptance closeout packet for the six pickups and storing it with the asset records, including warranty start dates. Extend the operating controls by adding charger inspection steps to the Facilities mobile checklist and requiring photo evidence for cabinet, cord, and bollard condition. Have Fleet produce a mid-pilot data-quality memo so any gaps in mileage, charging, or work-order coding are fixed before the TCO clock runs out.

periods.analysis: The pilot reached 25% complete, up from 22% by 3 percentage points quarter over quarter, and remains green. Charging depot site prep is still complete with dueOffsetDays -40, and Yard B charging assets are behaving like infrastructure rather than gadgets, which is the point. The first 6 EV pickups delivered milestone remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 35, with Fleet continuing to manage final acceptance and documentation for EV-PU-001 through EV-PU-006. The 12-month TCO comparison report remains not-started with dueOffsetDays 200, but the evidence base is now taking shape across routes, work orders, kWh, and avoided gasoline. At 25%, this is still a pilot, not a fleet conversion; that distinction protects the budget and the equipment.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green status by finishing the delivery acceptance file and reconciling each EV pickup’s asset record, charger assignment, operator cohort, and warranty terms. Extend the pilot carefully by identifying the next candidate use cases, but do not order additional units until the TCO report has enough operating months to support the ask. Prepare a Council-ready one-page dashboard showing percentComplete 25%, the 3 percentage point quarter-over-quarter movement, charger uptime, fleet availability, and open milestone status.

periods.analysis: 70% complete. 1 of 3 milestones are done. Next up: Charging depot site prep (due Oct 16, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
